an5.9:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing five qualities, an irreverent and undeferential bhikkhu falls away and is not established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:1.2: What five? (1) An irreverent and undeferential bhikkhu devoid of faith falls away and is not established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:1.3: (2) An irreverent and undeferential morally shameless bhikkhu …
an5.9:1.5: (3) An irreverent and undeferential morally reckless bhikkhu …
an5.9:1.6: (4) An irreverent and undeferential lazy bhikkhu …
an5.9:1.7: (5) An irreverent and undeferential unwise bhikkhu falls away and is not established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:1.8: Possessing these five qualities, an irreverent and undeferential bhikkhu is not established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:2.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing five other qualities, a reverential and deferential bhikkhu does not fall away but is established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:2.3: (1) A reverential and deferential bhikkhu endowed with faith does not fall away but is established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:2.4: (2) A reverential and deferential bhikkhu who has a sense of moral shame …
an5.9:2.5: (3) A reverential and deferential bhikkhu who has moral dread …
an5.9:2.6: (4) A reverential and deferential bhikkhu who is energetic …
an5.9:2.7: (5) A reverential and deferential bhikkhu who is wise does not fall away but is established in the good Dhamma.
an5.9:2.8: Possessing these five qualities, a reverential and deferential bhikkhu does not fall away but is established in the good Dhamma.”
